title: C declarations, declarators and type qualifiers reference
learningObjectives: Explain the topic and its C rules.
Trace the example and identify its purpose.
Identify important validation and failure cases.
Apply the concept in a tested program or reference exercise.

understand.concept: C declarations combine declaration specifiers and declarators to describe objects, functions and types. Declarators can include pointers, arrays and function forms; qualifiers such as const and volatile affect how objects may be accessed.
understand.whyItMatters: Reading complex declarations correctly is essential for understanding APIs, pointer types, function pointers and object mutability.
understand.analogy: Treat the project or language feature as a set of components with explicit interfaces and responsibilities.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy does not replace C's formal language, library and resource-management rules.

explain.narrative:
C declarations combine declaration specifiers and declarators to describe objects, functions and types. Declarators can include pointers, arrays and function forms; qualifiers such as const and volatile affect how objects may be accessed.

For a complete implementation, define input constraints, ownership, error handling and test cases before coding. Compile with warnings and verify normal, boundary and failure behaviour.

examples.title: Focused C example
examples.explanation: values is an array of four pointers to int. row is a pointer to an array of four int. read_only points to const int, while fixed is a const pointer to int.

practise.guidedTask: Read each declaration from the identifier outward and state its type.
practise.independentTask: Write declarations for an array of function pointers, a pointer to an array and a function returning a pointer.
hints: Parentheses can change declarator binding and therefore the declared type.
const placement changes whether the pointed-to object or the pointer itself is qualified.
Use typedef to clarify complex types without hiding important qualifiers.
